name: Flatback Syndrome
definition: Loss of normal lumbar lordosis causing positive sagittal imbalance, forward stooping and compensatory hip/knee flexion, often after prior fusion or degeneration.

investigations.principle: Standing full-spine radiographs with pelvic parameters are central; MRI/CT are used for neural and fusion assessment.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, occult injury, postoperative or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

green: Hip/core rehabilitation when flexible and stable
amber: Severe fixed sagittal imbalance may require complex deformity surgery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Prishtha-vakrata phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Loss of normal lumbar lordosis causing positive sagittal imbalance, forward stooping and compensatory hip/knee flexion, often after prior fusion or degeneration.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, respiratory distress, progressive neurological deficit, open injury, severe deformity, infection or other listed red flags.
